title: wolfHSM test suite: wp11_test_backend_wolfhsm.c with SHM loopback
description:
Create a test module for the wolfHSM backend. Tests must use an independent oracle — not the code under test as its own verifier.

Structure:
- test/wp11_test_backend_wolfhsm.c + test/wp11_test_backend_wolfhsm.h
- Start an in-process wolfHSM server using the SHM transport before tests run; tear it down after
- Provision known test keys on the server (reference vectors from NIST CAVS or RFC test vectors)

Test cases required:
1. sign_ecdsa_p256: Sign a known hash with a known P-256 key; verify the signature using wolfCrypt directly (not via wolfHSM backend) — cross-validation oracle
2. verify_ecdsa_p256: Pass a known-good signature to hsm_verify; check return == 0; pass a corrupted signature; check return < 0
3. decrypt_rsa_pkcs1: Encrypt a known plaintext with the RSA public key using wolfCrypt directly; pass ciphertext to hsm_decrypt; verify recovered plaintext matches
4. derive_ecdh_p256: Two keys on server; each derives with the other's public key; shared secrets must match (symmetry oracle identical to soft backend test)
5. error_notready: Simulate WH_ERROR_NOTREADY from the server (if wolfHSM server can be made to return this) and verify the backend returns WP11_BACKEND_ERR_NOT_READY; this covers wolfP11-8o2

Build gate: only compiled when WOLFHSM=1; guarded by WOLFP11_CFG_WOLFHSM_BACKEND.

Acceptance criteria:
- All 5 test cases pass with zero cross-validation discrepancies
- Test binary does not require a separate server process (in-process SHM server)
- wolfP11-8o2 (WH_ERROR_NOTREADY retry) is validated by test case 5 and can be closed
